description.narrative:
DisabiliTech 2.0 is a 12-month, youth-led AU–EU innovation project that strengthens the digital skills and employability of young persons with disabilities through inclusive capacity building and technology co-creation. The project delivers accessible training indata, AI, design, and web development, while engaging young persons with disabilities as co-designers of an accessibility-first digital learning mobile app. The app provides inclusive content on digital literacy, disability rights, employability, mental health,and life skills, featuring screen-reader compatibility, sign-language videos, audio learning, and offline access. Piloted in Nigeria through AU–EU youth collaboration, DisabiliTech 2.0 advances digital inclusion, youth innovation, and sustainable pathways for persons with disabilities to participate in the digital economy across Africa and Europe.
The goal is to enhance digital inclusion and employability of young Persons with Disabilities through inclusive skills development and technology innovation.
Objectives: 1. Buildinclusive digital, AI, design, and web skills among PWDs and youth 2. Co-create and develop an accessible digital learning app 3. Foster AU–EU youth innovation exchange
Activities of the project includes capacity-building training, participatory needs assessment, co-design workshops, app development and testing, pilot implementation, AU–EU knowledge exchange, advocacy, and sustainability planning.

participating-org.narrative:
The Special Physically Challenged Care Foundation, also known as “We Are Special,” is a disability-focused non-profit organisation committed to empowering, protecting, and advancing the rights, wellbeing, and dignity of persons with disabilities, with particular focus on girls and women. The organisation works to address systemic barriers through inclusive education, digital empowerment, advocacy, and sustainable development initiatives. It vision is a Nigeria where persons with disabilities, especially girls and women, are safe, fully included, protected from all forms of violence and discrimination and able to reach their full potential.
Guided by the principles of inclusion, equity, dignity, accountability, collaboration and respect for human rights, we are special seeks to expand access to quality inclusive education, strengthen economic and digital empowerment opportunities, promote disability rights andgender equity and support sustainable, inclusive community development.
The organization operates under a transparent, accountable, youth-led governance and management framework promoting inclusivity, innovation, and effective service delivery.
A youth-inclusive Board of Trustees, with three members under 30 and one above 35, provides strategic oversight. The Board appoints an Executive Director (27) supported by an Assistant Director (27) to lead strategy, partnerships, and daily operations.
Core functions of project coordination, administration, finance, M<(>&<)>E and HR are led by professionals aged 25–29. All staff are under 35, ensuring young people drive decision-making, implementation, and learning.
This structure ensures agility, peer-driven leadership, strong accountability, and programmes responsive to youth and community realities.
